sources.role: Pinnacle catalog entry; archive recorded as Pinnacle_V1.2.6_v.zip. The executable has not been inspected for equivalence.
Published average-gel, undecimated wavelet, peak detection and quantification algorithm.
sources.citation: Morris JS, Clark BN, Gutstein HB (2008). Pinnacle: a fast, automatic and accurate method for detecting and quantifying protein spots in 2-dimensional gel electrophoresis data. Bioinformatics 24:529–536. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btm590.

sources.role: Later GUI settings, regions, quantile background and normalization options. Identifies US patent 8,031,925.
Original RWT 2.4 source used for transform conventions and independent C references. Allocation-lifetime shim changes no transform arithmetic; complete license preserved.

implementation_choices: Separate published-paper and native-RWT noise/threshold settings; the paper MAD wording is interpreted as median-centered absolute deviation.
Periodic wavelet boundaries, explicit dyadic divisibility and no implicit padding.
Zero-based row/column coordinates, half-open regions, clipped windows, strict intensity threshold and descending-intensity greedy square suppression with lexicographic ties.
Streaming image passes, explicit bounds, immutable results and no silent clipping of negative background-corrected values.
Optional independent per-gel denoising during quantification requires explicit filter, threshold and paper/RWT convention; detection still uses the denoised raw average.

Background radius can be a (row, column) pair. Peak/background measurements use the optionally denoised crop; image-volume normalization uses the raw crop. This processing order is a Python convention pending executable confirmation.
limitations: Native TIFF/project-file ingestion, interactive peak editing, reports and Pinnacle executable equivalence remain open.
